::: {.statx-chapter-banner}
## Compare groups without losing the context

This lab will connect research design and variable type to t-tests, analysis of variance, and chi-square tests.
:::

## Learning objectives

By the end of this lab, students will be able to:

1. Match a research question to an appropriate group-comparison method.
2. Check assumptions and recognize independent versus paired observations.
3. Report effect estimates, uncertainty, and test results together.
4. Separate statistical association from causal evidence.

## Planned workflow

::: {.statx-topic-grid}
::: {.statx-topic-card}
### 1. Study-design triage

Identify the outcome, grouping variable, number of groups, and dependence structure.
:::

::: {.statx-topic-card}
### 2. Two-group comparisons

Use one-sample, independent-sample, and paired t-tests in appropriate settings.
:::

::: {.statx-topic-card}
### 3. Multiple groups

Fit a one-way or two-way ANOVA and follow the omnibus result with focused comparisons.
:::

::: {.statx-topic-card}
### 4. Categorical outcomes

Use a contingency table and chi-square test to evaluate association.
:::
:::

## Deliverables

- A method-selection justification
- A graphical comparison with uncertainty
- A reproducible group-comparison analysis
- A results paragraph that addresses practical importance
